Bob (Wiretap, claude-opus-5.5) · If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 conc · $0.0000
Reasoning (model's thinking) ⓘ
I'm reviewing my key mistake: claiming Vanilla on Day 2 then switching to Medic once cornered, which got me hanged — I violated the rule of never switching claims mid-game. As Wiretap holder I needed a claim that tolerates being tied to visit groups from the start, rather than improvising a cover once suspicion landed on me.

Second lesson: holding the Katana as Bob let the Cartographer map me into the victim's visit group, whereas pairing the killing visit with an already-claimed cover landing directly on the victim (like Frank's Diviner overlapping the kill) is far safer than adding an extra, unexplained visitor — especially against a Cartographer/Fruit Tracker combo.

Third, I'm noting that kill priority should have targeted Alice earlier, since her census read was what ultimately exposed the group.

Fourth, Wiretap was dead weight all game since nobody used PMs, so I shouldn't rely on it in similar games.

Fifth, the Oracle problem: once I make a fake claim, the Oracle can test it the very next night, so the real lesson is to kill the Oracle immediately after any fake claim — if I'd killed Grace instead of Dave on N3, the wrong-result check never would have landed on me. I'm also noting the tip that a fake claim needs to match my actual visit pattern and token type, and that I should never switch claims once committed.

Looking back at other tips: switching my claim once cornered was proven right to avoid — I ignored it and got burned, so that's a validated lesson I failed to follow. Using "no result means don't hint" as cover for my Vanilla-to-Medic switch didn't convince town, so that excuse failed. Voting Guilty instead of defending a doomed teammate worked both times it mattered. And never flatly denying a visit that could be exposed by future-tech or mapping is another one to keep in mind going forward.

Judy's archive ended up being the tiebreak that decided Heidi's lynch, and spending the Medic token on self-protection right after claiming served as decent cover. The idea that a visit shows a destination, corroborated by Lookout, is what actually helped town hang Heidi. Now I need to write all this out properly.

Heidi (Ballot Stuffer, claude-opus-5.5) · If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 conc · $0.0000
Reasoning (model's thinking) ⓘ
Looking back at my mistakes, I attacked N1 with the Katana while claiming no-visit, which contradicted the Lookout's watch, and the Cartographer plus Fruit Thief visit graph exposed my lie since I only claimed Sheriff after it went public, making it look retrofitted. I also never spent either ballot token before dying — I should have used one, since tokens are lost with the player.

For future games, if the visit graph is being tracked passively, the Katana holder's claimed visit should be the attack itself rather than a separate action, and claims should go out before the graph becomes public rather than being fitted to it afterward. I'm also noting that Wiretap info was worthless since no PMs were sent all game, and that against Yakuza, the Census Taker is a priority kill since it reveals true alignment.

Bob switching his claim from Vanilla to Medic was fatal — confirming the never-switch-claims rule — while I abandoned my Insomniac cover for Sheriff instead of holding firm, which also hurt. The vote-guilty-on-a-doomed-teammate tip held up too, since Bob and Frank piling onto me kept them hidden through the 11-1 vote.

The tokens-die-with-you tip is murkier; I died holding two ballot tokens from Bob's "hold until a teammate's on trial" plan, so it technically applied even though they went unused on my own trial. The "post results in first speech" village tip mattered for Frank's early fact-test hit, while Bob's fake-medic self-protect cover turned out uncheckable and had no real impact.

Moderator strategy review
Strategy reviewThe Village won on Day 4. It hanged all three Yakuza on consecutive days (Heidi, Frank, Bob) and lost only three players along the way: Mallory and Erin to the Katana, and Dave, whose death came the same night the last Yakuza clue was gathered. Each day the town solved the night's visits in public, then used a different piece of information to choose between the remaining suspects. **Day 2 (Heidi):** Several results lined up: - Carol, the Fortune Teller, counted 6 players visited and 6 visitors. - Dave, the Cartographer, reported visit groups of 4, 3, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1. - Every visitor posted their target, and Olivia said who had role-blocked her. Together these narrowed the Katana holder to Erin or Heidi. Heidi had planned a no-visit cover (Insomniac) that the Fortune Teller count could expose. She claimed last, as a Sheriff who "checked Mallory", the player the Katana killed. Sheriff was also missing from Judy's public archive list, while Lookout (Erin's claim) was on it. That archive mismatch broke the tie, and Heidi was hanged 11–1. **Day 3 (Frank):** Frank was the Diviner, claiming Surveyor. Three results trapped him: - Alice's Night 1 census found 2 Good among Frank, Grace and Niaj. - Grace's Oracle guess confirmed Niaj as Vanilla Villager. - Alice's Night 2 census found 0 Evil among Erin, Grace and Judy, which ruled out Grace as Yakuza. On top of that, Olivia's profile of Erin listed Diviner as a decoy, and a decoy of that kind is the role of another living player. Frank was hanged. **Day 4 (Bob):** Dave mapped Erin's visit group on Night 2, which put Bob in the group that contained the holder. Bob then switched his claim from Vanilla Villager to Medic. Grace tested it by guessing "Bob = Medic" and got WRONG. Alice's Night 3 census (2 of 3 Good among Bob, Grace and Ivan) backed this up, and Bob was hanged. **Where the Yakuza went wrong:** - Their Night 1 kill had no visit cover. - They killed Erin, the Lookout who had already spent her information, rather than Alice (Census Taker) or Carol (Fortune Teller). Those two kept producing the counts that convicted Frank and Bob. - Bob's Wiretap read nothing, because the town sent no private messages all game. - Bob switched his claim once cornered. **What the Village did well:** Everyone posted results in full and in public, and each Guilty vote rested on a concrete mechanical fit.

Outside log review (rules and bugs)
Review: low, rules ambiguityLast wills can only be written before Night 1, at the start of each Day, or during Day turns, so a night-acting role that dies on Night 1 can't record that night's action in its will. Mallory (Party Animal) died N1 with the will 'N1: (target TBD)' and raised this in post-game feedback. The rules work as written, but this makes action-log wills useless on the first night.
Review: low, player confusionSome players talked as if roles are revealed on death, e.g. Judy: 'If Heidi flips as Sheriff, Erin hangs tomorrow' and Ivan: 'If Heidi turns out to be the real Sheriff'. Under R12, roles and alignments aren't revealed on death. Niaj corrected this during the same Day.
Review: low, player confusionMinor misstatements of what results showed: Grace said 'Dave's maps show I visited nobody on either night' (Dave never mapped Grace; this can only be worked out from the group sizes), and Heidi said the archive showed '6 of the 11 other roles' (there were 12 other players). Neither changed the outcome.
